correctness.rationale: The unrestricted trace exponential has strictly positive Hessian in nonzero Laplacian directions, and edge weights map injectively to distinct offdiagonal entries; global uniqueness forces two edge-orbit rates. The tensor product yields eigenvalues 0,2b,ma,ma+2b with correct multiplicities. Scalar strict convexity plus verified exact one-sided derivatives gives necessary and sufficient complete price/time boundary conditions. Long-time and size laws follow algebraically from the interior equation and thresholds. The submitted verify.py replay returned VERIFY_OK 15520, corroborating but not replacing the proofs.

originality.rationale: The exact prism two-sided heat-trace support diagram, its threshold formulas, and the contrasting linear versus linear-logarithmic size scales were not found in the inspected primary sources or semantic published-finding corpus records. Same-graph prior resistance optimum has a different objective and always interior rates; generic convexity cannot imply the specific boundary phase law. A different-graph matching-premium heat-trace theorem cannot be restricted to prove optimum after deleting its other cross-edges. Unindexed equivalent work remains a risk.
residual_risks: A specialized heat-trace optimization theorem may exist outside indexed public archives, especially with alternate terminology such as thermal partition functions or graph communicability.
The original Boyd presentation gives a powerful general spectral-convexity framework; a prior unpublished elaboration might contain the same product calculation.
The publication date records the dated and publicly verifiable focal 2006 ICM presentation, not a claim that no related result was known earlier.

value.rationale: The two-clique perfect-matching design is a natural two-community control network. The complete all-budget price-time support classification shows a topologically meaningful phenomenon (disconnected finite-horizon optima on either side of unit price, but eventual activation of every link) absent from stationary resistance allocation. The different m versus m log m horizon scales quantify an actionable intervention boundary, not a tiny numerical gain or arbitrary parameter slice.
